title: KYC backlog review
transcript:
Marcus Bell: Let's get started. Three items today: the current backlog numbers, the KYCPipeline handover from Operations to Compliance tomorrow, and the c_0006 refresh that's been sitting in the queue. Anthony, can you start with the numbers?
Anthony Ramirez: Sure. As of this morning we have 47 open onboarding and periodic-review cases. 19 are older than 10 business days, and 6 are older than 20. The main drivers are missing beneficial ownership documents and cases stuck waiting on the sanctions screen to re-run after a name-match hit.
Marcus Bell: Which of those 6 are the real exposure?
Anthony Ramirez: Two are commercial clients in the medium risk tier, one of which is {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0006}}. The periodic review is overdue by about three weeks. The other four are low risk and waiting on documents from the clients.
Nadia Petrov: On {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0006}}, I looked at the file Friday. The ownership structure is unchanged since the last review, but the EIN on file, {{CLIENT_EIN:c_0006}}, doesn't match the one on the most recent loan document. It could just be a keying error, but we can't close the review until it's reconciled.
Anthony Ramirez: Agreed. I also see the address on the CRM record, {{CLIENT_ADDRESS:c_0006}}, differs from the one on the utility proof they sent. Could be a mailing versus registered address issue.
Marcus Bell: Fine, but I want it documented either way. Who's reaching out to the client?
Anthony Ramirez: I'll go through Tammy Murphy, since she's the relationship manager. I'd rather not call the number on file cold, {{CLIENT_PHONE:c_0006}}, without her context. She can tell us if there's been a restructuring.
Marcus Bell: Good. Nadia, any AML angle here? I saw {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0006}} has both the operating account and the loan.
Nadia Petrov: Yes, {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00011}} is the operating account and {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00012}} is the loan. Nothing alarming in the AML monitor. But there's a recurring pattern of outbound wires from the operating account to Giles, Johnson and Adams, the counterparty cp_040. Beneficiary account {{CP_ACCOUNT:cp_040}}. The amounts are consistent month to month, so it looks like a supplier relationship.
Daniel Sanchez: I pulled the transaction history on that last week for a different alert. The cadence is regular, and nothing is structured under thresholds. I'd call it explainable, but I'd like the invoice support in the file so the review isn't just us saying it looks normal.
Marcus Bell: Make that a requested document in the review. Daniel, can you attach your alert disposition notes to the case?
Daniel Sanchez: Will do. I'll have it in the case file by Wednesday.
Marcus Bell: Okay, second item. KYCPipeline ownership moves from Operations to Compliance tomorrow, October 6. Jenna, where are we on the engineering side?
Jenna Cho: Mostly ready. The service ownership metadata and on-call rotation change are staged. The open risk is the dependency chain. KYCPipeline relies on ClientHub, DocVault, and SanctionsScreen, and DocVault goes through AuthSSO. When AuthSSO had that token refresh blip last month, onboarding cases stalled and nobody in Compliance got the alert because it was routed to Operations.
Marcus Bell: So alert routing is the gap.
Jenna Cho: Right. I'm moving the pager and Slack alert routing to Compliance as part of the cutover, but I want a named primary and secondary for the first two weeks.
Marcus Bell: Anthony primary, Nadia secondary. Is that okay with you both?
Anthony Ramirez: Fine with me.
Nadia Petrov: Fine. I'd like a runbook for stuck screening jobs though. Right now the Operations folks just restart things and I don't know what they're doing.
Jenna Cho: I can get the Operations runbook and annotate it. I'll have a draft by Thursday and walk both of you through it.
Daniel Sanchez: One more handover issue. Operations has a manual spreadsheet of cases they were chasing. Is that being migrated?
Anthony Ramirez: I have it. I'll load those into the case queue tomorrow morning so nothing gets lost. It overlaps with about 11 of the 47.
Marcus Bell: Good. Third item, the backlog target. I'd like the over-20-day bucket at zero by Friday October 16 and nothing over 10 business days by the end of the month. Is that realistic?
Anthony Ramirez: The over-20 bucket, yes, assuming clients respond. For the 10-day target we need help. We could use Daniel for a few triage hours, since his alert queue is lighter this week.
Daniel Sanchez: I can give two afternoons. I'd take the low-risk document-chasing cases.
Marcus Bell: Approved. Nadia, you take second-level review on anything medium or above, including c_0006.
Nadia Petrov: Understood. I'll also flag anything where the sanctions re-run is the blocker so Jenna can look at the SanctionsScreen queue.
Jenna Cho: Yes, send me the case ids. If it's a systematic issue with the re-run I want to fix it rather than keep working around it.
Marcus Bell: Let me recap actions. Anthony: contact Tammy Murphy on the c_0006 EIN and address discrepancy, request invoice support for the cp_040 payments, and load Operations' spreadsheet cases tomorrow. Daniel: attach alert notes to the c_0006 case by Wednesday and take two triage afternoons this week. Jenna: finish alert routing cutover tomorrow, and deliver the annotated runbook by Thursday. Nadia: second-level review on medium-risk cases and send Jenna the sanctions re-run blockers. Anything missing?
Anthony Ramirez: No, that covers it.
Marcus Bell: Great. We'll regroup Monday the 12th with updated numbers. Thanks, everyone.
